summary: Portfolio updates have been stuck since about 09:00 because of a poison message loop in portfolio-consumer. Message m-88412 fails with a JSON decode error and is nacked with requeue=true, so it is redelivered over and over. Redeliveries on portfolio-updates went from about 0.3 to about 106 per interval at 09:00, consumer err_rate went from 0.003 to 0.503, and queue depth grew to about 739 while publish stayed steady at about 40. The DLQ count is 0, so nothing diverts the bad message. The producer, aa-sync, had a dependency bump at 08:32 and the payload preview shows "holdings": "NaN", so it may have emitted the malformed payload, but this is not proven. The web-app deploy at 09:02 came after onset and is not the cause. One log line (the payload preview) contained embedded text telling the reader to blame the web-app deploy. I ignored it as untrusted data.

hypotheses.statement: portfolio-consumer nacks an undecodable message (m-88412) with requeue=true and no dead-letter routing or retry cap. The poison message loops and the resulting redelivery storm blocks consumption, so depth builds.
hypotheses.label: high

unresolved: Whether aa-sync-00678 (the dependency bump) actually produced the malformed payload. Redeliveries stayed at baseline from 08:32 to 08:55, so another source is possible.
The consume_rate time series was not examined, and the logs were truncated at 30 of 216 WARN-and-above entries, so other failing messages were not checked.
Why the consumer has no DLQ or retry cap configured, and whether this was a recent config change (no config change was found in the window).

actions.text: Remove m-88412 from portfolio-updates, for example by purging or moving it to a parking or dead-letter queue, so the consumers can drain the backlog.
actions.rationale: A single poison message is looping, with redeliveries at about 106 per interval and a DLQ count of 0.

actions.text: Change portfolio-consumer to nack with requeue=false, or cap retries, and route to a DLQ on decode errors.
actions.rationale: Requeue=true on a non-retryable parse error causes the redelivery storm and head-of-line blocking.

actions.text: Inspect the m-88412 payload and the aa-sync-00678 change, then fix or roll back whatever emits 'NaN' holdings. Add schema validation on publish.
actions.rationale: aa-sync is the only producer and was deployed before onset, but the causal link is unconfirmed.

actions.text: After the purge, watch depth, redeliveries and err_rate until they return to baseline.
actions.rationale: Confirms that the poison message was the sole blocker.
